idiom_name: typed document + explicit schema/serializer at a message endpoint
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define the document as a schema (record, struct or IDL type) separate from the domain model, add a version or format header, and give each endpoint the two mappings it owns - domain object to document on the sending side, document to whatever the receiver needs on the receiving side. Serialize at the boundary with an explicit encoder (JSON text, protobuf or fixed binary, XML), never by dumping internal object graphs; validate on decode and route rejects to an error channel. Receiver code selects behavior from document content and type, not from a shared class hierarchy, because there is no operation name to dispatch on. Delivery guarantees, ordering and idempotency are configured on the channel, not in the document. When using schema registries (Confluent, Apicurio), register schemas before deployment and configure compatibility mode (BACKWARD recommended as default); for Avro use union-with-null for optional fields with default values; for Protobuf use optional fields and reserve retired field numbers. For idempotent consumption, record a stable message deduplication key (e.g., business ID or source+sequence) in the same transaction as business writes.
code_sketch:
document OrderShipped { version: 3, order_id: string, lines: [Line], shipped_at: timestamp }

send:    msg = encode(OrderShipped, mapper.to_document(order))   # JSON or binary + headers
         channel.send(msg)
receive: doc = validate(decode(headers.format, body))
         for each receiver_rule matching doc:       # receiver decides; no operation name
             apply(doc) | store(doc) | ignore()
         on reject: error_channel.send(body, reason)
pitfalls: Encoding internal domain objects implicitly via reflection serializes the producer's internal model as the wire contract, making every refactor silently break consumers.
Publishing a document without a version or format marker causes newer producer documents to be silently misread by older consumers that cannot parse new fields or types.
A document without an invalid-message or dead-letter channel endpoint ends up dropped in a production backlog that nobody monitors, creating silent data loss.
Schema breaking changes — removing mandatory fields, changing types, renaming elements — without a versioned topic strategy or migration plan breaks existing consumers immediately on deployment.

Non-idempotent consumers receiving at-least-once delivery without a deduplication key causes duplicate processing: every consumer must check for existence of a stable business key before applying the document.

Publishing full internal entity state when only delta or relevant fields are needed bloats payloads, leaks internal details that couple producers to consumers permanently, and pressures broker memory and CPU.
Oversized documents exceeding broker limits without a Claim Check cause message broker rejections or memory pressure; define a payload size budget per document type and enforce it in CI.
Consumer-side schema guessing: relying on optional fields being absent rather than explicitly checking version causes silent misreads when a newer producer begins emitting previously absent fields.
Using a shared message channel as the system of record for in-flight documents rather than persisting authoritative state in a database first — the channel should transport data, not hold it.
No monitoring on dead-letter queue depth: documents that fail validation accumulate silently in DLQ while operators believe the pipeline is healthy, causing data gaps discovered only on audit.
Publishing sensitive fields (PII, credentials, internal IDs) in documents without field-level encryption or redaction couples producers to compliance requirements and leaks data to any consumer.

Version skew between producer schema and consumer interpretation during rolling deployments: a new producer can start writing in a new format before all consumers have migrated, causing partial failures.

Wrong move: publishing documents to a Publish-Subscribe channel by default -> every subscriber keeps its own read-only copy, data duplicates and silently diverges -> instead default to a Point-to-Point channel and use Publish-Subscribe only when several independent consumers genuinely need to decide separately.

Wrong move: designing one generic all-purpose document envelope that accumulates every field any consumer might want -> the god-message junk drawer hides coupling behind a bloated payload and every consumer re-derives meaning from the pile -> instead define one schema per document kind and bind each kind to its own datatype channel.

Wrong move: making downstream systems subscribe to the producer's process events and call back for the full data -> every consumer couples to the producer's business process and breaks when its rules change -> instead publish the authoritative business document (invoice, despatch advice) carrying a correlation id so receivers apply their own rules.
